_meta.purpose: Machine-readable start point for the #606 Shadow-binding law: a closure packet whose shadow_review.verdict is PASS must name a Shadow identity distinct from the packet author and a receipt that exists at its bound sha256. This file lists the packets that were already green under the unbound rule, so history stays honest and every new packet is bound.
_meta.why_not_backfill: The Shadow that reviewed these packets left no recorded identity or receipt. Writing one now would be invention, and inventing a reviewer is exactly the promotion #606 exists to stop. Flipping their verdicts to HUMAN_ADMIT_REQUIRED would be the opposite invention: it would claim we know the review did not happen.
_meta.why_a_list_and_not_a_date: A closure packet has no intrinsic ordering the gate can read, unlike a commit. Listing the grandfathered packets one by one keeps the gate blocking for everything else, and the length of this list is the honest measure of how many PASS verdicts in the ledger are still self-signed.
_meta.how_to_stop_adding_to_this: Nothing may be added. A new packet binds its Shadow, or it records HUMAN_ADMIT_REQUIRED. An entry here admits one exact file name at one exact Issue number with one exact verdict; changing any of the three drops the packet out of the grandfathered set and the binding is required again.
